facts: The reference angle $A=\tan^{-1}\frac{|y|}{|x|}$ is always acute, because the absolute values remove the signs.
By quadrant, $\theta=A$, $180^{\circ}-A$, $180^{\circ}+A$ or $360^{\circ}-A$ for quadrants $1$, $2$, $3$ and $4$.
A calculator returns $\tan^{-1}$ between $-90^{\circ}$ and $90^{\circ}$, so it never gives a second- or third-quadrant angle directly.
A **true bearing** is measured clockwise from north, so $\text{bearing}=90^{\circ}-\theta$, adding $360^{\circ}$ if that is negative.
A bearing and an angle of inclination are different numbers for the same vector, so read which one is wanted.
A vector and its negative point opposite ways, so their angles of inclination differ by $180^{\circ}$.
steps: Sketch the vector and name the quadrant it lies in.
Use the quadrant to write the angle of inclination $\theta$.
Convert to a true bearing with $\text{bearing}=90^{\circ}-\theta$ if the question asks for one.

foundation.question_text: Find the angle of inclination of $\underset{\sim}{a}=\begin{pmatrix}5\\2\end{pmatrix}$, to the nearest degree.
foundation.solution_text:
Both components are positive, so the vector lies in the first quadrant.
$A=\tan^{-1}\frac{2}{5}$
$=21.80^{\circ}$
$\theta=A$
$\approx 22^{\circ}$

foundation.question_text: Find the angle of inclination of $\underset{\sim}{a}=-4\underset{\sim}{i}+3\underset{\sim}{j}$, to the nearest degree.
Find the exact angle of inclination of $\underset{\sim}{b}=\begin{pmatrix}-6\\-6\end{pmatrix}$.
foundation.solution_text:
Both components are negative, so the vector lies in the third quadrant.
$A=\tan^{-1}\frac{6}{6}$
$=45^{\circ}$
$\theta=180^{\circ}+45^{\circ}$
$=225^{\circ}$

foundation.question_text: Find the angle of inclination of $\underset{\sim}{c}=7\underset{\sim}{i}-4\underset{\sim}{j}$, to the nearest degree.
foundation.solution_text:
Here $x>0$ and $y<0$, so the vector lies in the fourth quadrant.
$A=\tan^{-1}\frac{4}{7}$
$=29.74^{\circ}$
$\theta=360^{\circ}-29.74^{\circ}$
$\approx 330^{\circ}$

foundation.question_text:
The vector $\underset{\sim}{a}=4\underset{\sim}{i}+4\underset{\sim}{j}$ is drawn with $\underset{\sim}{i}$ pointing east and $\underset{\sim}{j}$ pointing north.
Find the direction of $\underset{\sim}{a}$ as a true bearing.

The vector $\underset{\sim}{b}=\begin{pmatrix}-8\\15\end{pmatrix}$ is drawn with $\underset{\sim}{i}$ pointing east and $\underset{\sim}{j}$ pointing north.
Find the direction of $\underset{\sim}{b}$ as a true bearing, to the nearest degree.
foundation.solution_text:
Here $x<0$ and $y>0$, so the vector lies in the second quadrant.
$A=\tan^{-1}\frac{15}{8}$
$=61.93^{\circ}$
$\theta=180^{\circ}-61.93^{\circ}$
$=118.07^{\circ}$
$\text{bearing}=90^{\circ}-118.07^{\circ}$
$=-28.07^{\circ}$
$=-28.07^{\circ}+360^{\circ}$
$\approx 332^{\circ}\text{T}$

development.question_text: Find the exact angle of inclination of $\underset{\sim}{b}=2\underset{\sim}{i}-2\sqrt{3}\,\underset{\sim}{j}$.
development.solution_text:
Here $x>0$ and $y<0$, so the vector lies in the fourth quadrant.
$A=\tan^{-1}\frac{2\sqrt{3}}{2}$
$=\tan^{-1}\sqrt{3}$
$=60^{\circ}$
$\theta=360^{\circ}-60^{\circ}$
$=300^{\circ}$

$\theta=180^{\circ}-60^{\circ}$

development.question_text: Given $\underset{\sim}{a}=\begin{pmatrix}4\\7\end{pmatrix}$ and $\underset{\sim}{b}=\begin{pmatrix}-9\\-2\end{pmatrix}$, find the exact angle of inclination of $\underset{\sim}{a}+\underset{\sim}{b}$.
development.solution_text:
$\underset{\sim}{a}+\underset{\sim}{b}=\begin{pmatrix}4+(-9)\\7+(-2)\end{pmatrix}$
$=\begin{pmatrix}-5\\5\end{pmatrix}$
Here $x<0$ and $y>0$, so the vector lies in the second quadrant.
$A=\tan^{-1}\frac{5}{5}$
$=45^{\circ}$
$\theta=180^{\circ}-45^{\circ}$
$=135^{\circ}$

development.question_text:
The vector $\underset{\sim}{d}=-3\underset{\sim}{i}-4\underset{\sim}{j}$ is drawn with $\underset{\sim}{i}$ pointing east and $\underset{\sim}{j}$ pointing north.
Find the direction of $\underset{\sim}{d}$ as a true bearing, to the nearest degree.
development.solution_text:
Both components are negative, so the vector lies in the third quadrant.
$A=\tan^{-1}\frac{4}{3}$
$=53.13^{\circ}$
$\theta=180^{\circ}+53.13^{\circ}$
$=233.13^{\circ}$
$\text{bearing}=90^{\circ}-233.13^{\circ}$
$=-143.13^{\circ}$
$=-143.13^{\circ}+360^{\circ}$
$\approx 217^{\circ}\text{T}$

Given $\underset{\sim}{p}=\underset{\sim}{i}+6\underset{\sim}{j}$ and $\underset{\sim}{q}=4\underset{\sim}{i}+2\underset{\sim}{j}$, find the angle of inclination of $\underset{\sim}{p}-\underset{\sim}{q}$, to the nearest degree.
development.solution_text:
$\underset{\sim}{p}-\underset{\sim}{q}=(1-4)\underset{\sim}{i}+(6-2)\underset{\sim}{j}$
$=-3\underset{\sim}{i}+4\underset{\sim}{j}$
Here $x<0$ and $y>0$, so the vector lies in the second quadrant.
$A=\tan^{-1}\frac{4}{3}$
$=53.13^{\circ}$
$\theta=180^{\circ}-53.13^{\circ}$
$\approx 127^{\circ}$

mastery.solution_text:
$2\underset{\sim}{a}=12\underset{\sim}{i}-2\underset{\sim}{j}$
$3\underset{\sim}{b}=-6\underset{\sim}{i}+15\underset{\sim}{j}$

$=18\underset{\sim}{i}-17\underset{\sim}{j}$
Here $x>0$ and $y<0$, so the vector lies in the fourth quadrant.
$A=\tan^{-1}\frac{17}{18}$
$=43.36^{\circ}$
$\theta=360^{\circ}-43.36^{\circ}$
